title: Determination of toxic comments and unintended model bias minimization using Deep learning approach
findings: The study found that religious identities such as Muslim and Jewish were among the most frequently targeted in toxic comments. The fine-tuned BERT model significantly outperformed the Logistic Regression model in both overall toxicity classification and in minimizing unintended bias against religious identity groups. BERT demonstrated higher scores across bias metrics (subgroup-AUC, BPSN-AUC, and BNSP-AUC) for comments mentioning Christian, Muslim, and Jewish identities, indicating it was better at distinguishing toxic comments from non-toxic comments that simply mention a religious group.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured unintended model bias against religious identity terms (e.g., Muslim, Jewish, Christian) in the context of toxic comment classification. The goal was to evaluate how well models could identify toxicity without unfairly penalizing non-toxic comments that mention these religious identities.
